subject: Welcome to TXKPRO Workforce — build skills into opportunity
heading: Thanks for joining us.
body: Thanks for joining TXKPRO Workforce as a student or learner. We are building the program to help skilled-career learners make their abilities easier to see through projects, work samples, credentials, experience, and other evidence of what they can do.
notes: Sent immediately after explicit Workforce email opt-in.

subject: Two minutes can help shape TXKPRO Workforce
heading: Where is the real need?
body: Your answers can help us understand where learners lose momentum before training, during training, and when trying to move into work.
notes: Used when the subscriber has not completed the survey.

subject: Could we learn from your experience?
heading: Help us understand the workflow.
body: A short conversation can help us understand the context behind the barriers learners experience and the workarounds they use today.
notes: Used when the subscriber has not booked an interview.

subject: Thank you for helping shape TXKPRO Workforce
heading: What happens next
body: We are turning learner feedback into clearer priorities for profiles, opportunity discovery, support resources, and the transition from training into work.
notes: Fallback/progress email after research invitations.

subject: What we are learning through TXKPRO Workforce research
heading: Evidence before assumptions.
body: We are continuing to compare what different parts of the local workforce system are experiencing so we can identify needs that repeat across groups. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: research_update

subject: What we are hearing from the local workforce
heading: Patterns are starting to emerge.
body: The most useful feedback is showing us where people lose momentum between awareness, training, proof of skills, hiring, and ongoing support. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: what_we_heard

subject: Why proof of work may matter more than another résumé
heading: Show the work.
body: One area we are exploring is how projects, credentials, photos, videos, and other evidence can make practical ability easier to understand. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: work_profile

subject: Making local opportunities easier to find and act on
heading: Reduce the distance to opportunity.
body: A recurring design question is how to connect the right local opportunity with the right person without creating another complicated job board. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: local_opportunity

subject: The barrier may happen before the application
heading: Look earlier in the journey.
body: Cost, transportation, scheduling, awareness, confidence, and access to support can prevent progress long before someone reaches an employer. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: barrier_focus

subject: TXKPRO Workforce pilot participation
heading: Help us test the direction.
body: As the program becomes more concrete, we are identifying people and organizations willing to test workflows and tell us where the experience breaks down. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: pilot_invite

subject: Closing the loop between training and employer needs
heading: Training and hiring should inform each other.
body: We are exploring how employer expectations and training outcomes can be made more visible without adding administrative burden to either side. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: employer_training_connection

subject: TXKPRO Workforce progress update
heading: Building from the evidence.
body: We are translating interviews, survey responses, and workflow observations into clearer priorities for the Workforce program. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: program_progress

subject: Early TXKPRO Workforce participation
heading: Early access is getting closer.
body: We are preparing the program for more structured testing and will prioritize people who have helped us understand the problem space. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: early_access

subject: A look toward the TXKPRO Workforce launch
heading: From research to launch.
body: As March approaches, the focus is shifting from broad discovery toward readiness, onboarding, and the workflows participants will use first. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: launch_preview

subject: A workforce system is more than jobs and training
heading: Support systems matter.
body: The local workforce journey also depends on families, transportation, community organizations, financial support, mentors, and other resources around the learner and employer. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: community_signal

subject: The next TXKPRO Workforce build decisions
heading: What should come first?
body: We are prioritizing the smallest set of capabilities that can improve the transition between learning, evidence of skill, local opportunity, and employer action. For learners, we are especially looking at what makes it easier to show practical ability and move confidently toward the next step.
notes: Role-specific campaign content for theme: next_step

body: Your answers can help us identify where the greatest local workforce gaps may lie and which outcomes should be prioritized first.
notes: Used when the subscriber has not completed the survey.

subject: Could we learn from your experience?
heading: Help us understand the workflow.

notes: Used when the subscriber has not booked an interview.

subject: Thank you for helping shape TXKPRO Workforce
heading: What happens next
body: We are combining feedback across learners, families, employers, instructors, and community partners to decide what TXKPRO should build first.

subject: What we are learning through TXKPRO Workforce research
heading: Evidence before assumptions.
body: We are continuing to compare what different parts of the local workforce system are experiencing so we can identify needs that repeat across groups. Broad community feedback is helping us see which gaps are shared across multiple parts of the local workforce system.

subject: What we are hearing from the local workforce
heading: Patterns are starting to emerge.
body: The most useful feedback is showing us where people lose momentum between awareness, training, proof of skills, hiring, and ongoing support. Broad community feedback is helping us see which gaps are shared across multiple parts of the local workforce system.
